object.name: evi.valve~
object.description: Antialiased diode distortion with dynamic envelope following network based around vactrol emulation as well as asymmetric processing. The object is like a guitar pre-amp with Baxandall EQ and high gain (scream/sustain) capabilities, but has been tuned with options to work on all sorts of input material. It is of course very expensive to compute.
object.discussion: It started on this thread in 2012: https://cycling74.com/forums/valve-distortion . Thanks to Rodrigo Constanzo and Peter McCulloch.

inlets.description: Input audio will be followed and saturated.

outlets.description: The gain envelope used in the dynamic gain control into the core saturation unit. Is time aligned with the output (is delayed).
The output of evi.valve~ is delayed by this amount of samples. Use this value to delay your dry audio chain if in a mix situation.

messages.name: history
messages.digest: Top level gen~ [history] / History() declarations can be reset by messages to the object

attributes.name: asymmetry
attributes.description: This is actually 'fake' dB but has a similar effect. Asymmetry always favours negative over positive waveform, but this control changes the relationship between them. It also ultimately adds gain to the signal before the saturation stage, so could be seen as an addition to @bass and @treble.

attributes.name: bass
attributes.description: Input gain to the saturator, bass focussed, part of the 'Baxandall' EQ on the pre-amp along with the @treble attribute.

attributes.name: compensate
attributes.description: Compensate high frequency content. Marketing people would call this control 'air'. It basically high-shelf-boosts the high frequencies above 6kHz. This is mainly useful in restoring high details lost in the antiderivative antialiasing and oversampling algorithms.

attributes.name: diode
attributes.description: Effectively diode 'type' used in the valve distortion. '1' ('hard', default, most expensive to compute) is an agressive and faithful emulation of an analog diode. '0' ('soft', cheaper to compute) is a 'diode-like' nonlinearity which when pushed hard is diode-like in shape, but with less gain rolls off more smoothly.

attributes.name: envasym
attributes.description: This @envasym attribute turns the envelope follower gain at the asymmetry stage on or off. If one of the @envasym or @envvalve attributes is active, we have a single dynamic gain envelope (normal operation), if both attributes are active we have double envelope gain staging before the saturation stage which can be extreme in effect. If both attributes are off we have no dynamic gain envelopes and have a quasi 'static' distortion unit (not really the point of evi.valve~).

attributes.name: envattack
attributes.description: Envelope detection attack time in samples. Not a plain 'attack' as this is affected by other attributes such as @envinterval and @envshape.

attributes.name: envinterval
attributes.description: The averaging period in samples of the internal envelope follower averaging, and therefore also the entire object latency (reported out the far right outlet). Shorter values are generally better for more transient material, longer values for more sustained material, but always worth experimenting as interesting hysterisis effects can be achieved if forcing this value to be quirky sizes.

attributes.name: envrelease
attributes.description: Envelope detection release time in samples. Not a plain 'release' as the response of the envelope is affected by other attributes such as @envinterval and @envshape.

attributes.name: envscale
attributes.description: Scales the main gain envelope. At '0.' the envelope is at it's most dynamic, the higher this attribute value the more compressed the envelope is, but also the highjer gain the envelope is on average. Higher values mean a higher gain floor.

attributes.name: envshape
attributes.description: Transform the envelope shape between flat ('0') and sharp('1'). This controls the frequency response of the internal vactrol filters.

attributes.name: envvalve
attributes.description: This @envvalve attribute turns the envelope follower gain at the core saturation stage on or off. If one of the @envasym or @envvalve attributes is active, we have a single dynamic gain envelope (normal operation), if both attributes are active we have double envelope gain staging before the saturation stage which can be extreme in effect. If both attributes are off we have no dynamic gain envelopes and have a quasi 'static' distortion unit (not really the point of evi.valve~).

attributes.name: highpass
attributes.description: Final highpass filter on the output to help tame the bass.

attributes.name: hysterisis
attributes.description: Amount of hysterisis present in the pre (asymmetry) / post (nonlinear lowpass) saturation stages. If '0.' there are no hysterisis envelopes, at '1.' there is the most interference from the hysterisis envelopes.

attributes.name: makeup
attributes.description: Makeup gain in dB. This is very dangerous, as it is post saturation and so you could clip the output. Required sometimes depending on envelope settings and input material. Use with great care!

attributes.name: treble
attributes.description: Input gain to the saturator, treble focussed, part of the 'Baxandall' EQ on the pre-amp along with the @bass attribute.
